### Policies and issues related to the development and operationalization of the Trans-Asian Railway Network

Note by the secretariat

Summary

To ensure the sustainability of transport while meeting increasing freight and passenger demand in Asia and the Pacific, rail must assume a greater role in the region. In the present document, the secretariat highlights recent key developments among members of the Trans-Asian Railway Network and outlines strategies to further enhance the competitiveness and sustainability of rail transport to support the realization of the three interrelated objectives of the Regional Action Programme for Sustainable Transport Development in Asia and the Pacific (2022–2026). For realizing the first objective (efficient and resilient transport and logistics networks and mobility for economic growth), there is a continued need to prioritize the construction of key missing links on the Trans-Asian Railway Network and to address rail operational connectivity issues by leveraging digitalization. Enhanced intra- and inter-subregional rail connectivity constitutes another focus area; in this regard, the secretariat describes the ongoing work on strengthening rail interoperability among States members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and enhancing rail connectivity between South-East Asia and North and Central Asia. Furthermore, to enable seamless connectivity between disparate railway systems along the Network, a railway connectivity standards scheme is contained in the annex to the present document for the consideration of the Working Group. The scheme includes a proposal for the establishment of a task force operating under the Working Group on the Trans-Asian Railway Network. For addressing the second and third objectives (environmentally sustainable transport systems and services; and safe and inclusive transport and mobility), the secretariat emphasizes the need to expand regional cooperation on high-speed and urban rail and to address the threats posed by climate change to rail infrastructure. Furthermore, it describes the potential of rail to make transport more inclusive by instituting proactive measures to increase the participation of women in rail in the region.

Against this background, the Working Group may wish to provide additional guidance to the secretariat on policies and issues related to the development and operationalization of the Trans-Asian Railway Network, including in relation to: (a) Exploring innovative approaches for the construction of missing links along the Trans-Asian Railway Network; (b) Accelerating rail digitalization and enhancing intra- and inter subregional rail connectivity, including through the formulation of a strategic plan on enhancing rail interoperability among ASEAN member States and a road map on strengthening rail connectivity between South-East Asia and North and Central Asia;

(c) Heightening regional cooperation in the development of high-speed rail and urban transit and enhancing the resilience of rail transport infrastructure to the impacts of climate change; (d) Enhancing the inclusiveness of rail transport by promoting greater coordination on urban rail development and increasing the role of women in rail through proactive policy measures. The Working Group may also wish to consider adopting the railway connectivity standards scheme contained in the annex to the present document.

### I. Introduction

1. Transport demand in Asia and the Pacific will continue on its upward trajectory given the underlying need for economic growth in order to meet outstanding development challenges. According to the Asian Transport Observatory, passenger and freight activity are projected to grow by 30 per cent and 60 per cent, respectively, over the period from 2020 to 2030, 1 and carbon dioxide emissions are expected to rise by 20 per cent over the same period. Another study by the Asian Transport Observatory indicates that meeting transport demand in the Asia-Pacific region between 2020 and 2035 would require an investment of $43 trillion to develop, maintain and repair transport infrastructure and that, based on historical trends, the share of road transport in such investment would be an estimated 63 per cent, compared with 28 per cent for rail, including rapid urban transit. 2 That works out to an investment in rail, including high-speed and urban rail, of around $800 billion annually. With such massive investments expected to flow into the rail sector, it is imperative that rail policymakers in the region are equipped, in terms of knowledge and skills, to fully harness the potential of rail as an energy-efficient and environmentally friendly mode of transport. Efficient rail transport is also key to address rising carbon dioxide emissions from road freight transport in the region, which are estimated to account for 57 per cent of all transport carbon dioxide emissions by 2030.

2. In addition, a major trend that has taken shape over the past decade is the increasing role of rail in the transport of goods between Asia and Europe. The number of freight train trips made between the two continents has risen exponentially, from 17 in 2011 to around 17,000 in 2023. The coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic accelerated the usage of rail as established shipping routes faced major disruptions. Moreover, lingering geopolitical challenges have encouraged countries to diversify their transport linkages, leading to increased investment in rail infrastructure in many countries, in

Together, these factors have supported the establishment of rail as a reliable and sustainable transport connectivity option for transporting goods between Asia and Europe along the corridors of the Trans-Asian Railway Network. To strengthen this trend, it is imperative to further enhance the competitiveness of railway transport. In this regard, the Trans-Asian Railway Network has played, and could continue to play, a pivotal role.

3. The Trans-Asian Railway Network was established by the members of the Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP) after decades of efforts that culminated in the formalization of the Network in 2006 through the Intergovernmental Agreement on the Trans-Asian Railway Network. The Network passes through 28 countries and the number of Parties to the Agreement stands at 22 in 2025. The remaining non-Party States are actively considering becoming Parties to the Agreement, recognizing the growing importance of the Network in fostering regional transport connectivity in general and rail connectivity in particular.

4. A central factor underpinning the growing significance of the Network is the rapid expansion of Eurasian rail traffic over the past decade, which has resulted in an increasing number of countries participating in international rail traffic. It is increasingly common for freight trains to cross not one but multiple countries to transport goods between Asia and Europe. These rail interconnections have increased interdependencies, and disruptions in one country may have cascading effects along the entire corridor or network. In such situations, the Trans-Asian Railway Network offers a framework for developing a better understanding of these interdependencies through a systems approach. For instance, the operationalization of the rail link between China and the Lao People’s Democratic Republic is having an influence on rail investment strategies in South-East Asian countries and has potential implications for countries in North and Central Asia, given the enhanced feasibility of transporting goods between the two subregions. Consequently, it is imperative that, when rail investment plans are being formulated, a comprehensive analysis of the impacts arising from changes along the Network is conducted and strategies are adjusted as appropriate.

5. Since the eighth meeting of the Working Group on the Trans-Asian Railway Network, held in Bangkok and online on 14 and 15 September 2023, the importance of the Trans-Asian Railway Network and issues related to its further development and operationalization have been mentioned during the discussions at intergovernmental meetings, namely the eighth session of the Committee on Transport, held in Bangkok in November 2024. The Committee took note of the adoption by the Working Group at its eighth meeting of (a) the new annex to the Intergovernmental Agreement on the Trans-Asian Railway Network, on general principles on electronic information exchange among railways and between railways and control agencies; and (b) the Strategy 2030 on Accelerating Rail Digital Transformation in the Asia-Pacific Region.

6. In addition, the secretariat has leveraged existing partnerships to further promote regional and global rail transport collaboration. Issues of common interest and synergies have been discussed at various meetings and events since the eighth meeting of the Working Group, including (a) a meeting on the development of measures aimed at the facilitation of border-crossing procedures for international railway traffic in Eurasia, held in Warsaw and online from 27 to 29 May 2025 and organized by the Organization for Cooperation between Railways; (b) the fifth meeting of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) railway sub-working group, held in Siem

Reap, Cambodia, on 10 and 11 September 2024 and organized by the ASEAN secretariat; (c) the Fifteenth Regional Environmentally Sustainable Transport Forum in Asia, held in Kuala Lumpur from 24 to 26 October 2023 and organized by the United Nations Centre for Regional Development; and (d) the first Asia-Pacific Rail Summit, held in Kuala Lumpur on 23 October 2023 and organized by the International Union of Railways.

### II. Current state of the Trans-Asian Railway Network and recent rail developments among its members

7. Together with the Asian Highway Network and the network of dry ports of international importance, the Trans-Asian Railway Network provides the backbone for an integrated, intermodal transport system for the region. Measuring approximately 134,000 km in length, the Network is spread across 28 countries in the region and provides links to Europe. Over the past decade, growing Eurasian rail traffic has led to substantial investments to further improve rail infrastructure in many countries. Some of the significant developments among the members of the Trans-Asian Railway Network over past two years are described in the following paragraphs.

8. In June 2024, an intergovernmental agreement between China, Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan was signed for the construction of a new railway connecting the three countries. The agreement lays out principles and mechanisms for cooperation among the three countries for the financing, construction, operation and maintenance of the rail line. The proposed railway line would create a new rail transport corridor between East Asia and Central Asia and onward to Europe.
